areas.title: Forerunner can keep a noticeboard on GitHub: list an issue's comments with their authors, edit its own comment, pin the issue, read cheaply with ETags and know when issues are off, on GitHub and on both stand-ins
problems: [major, never cut] W8-host-1: The GitHost port cannot keep a noticeboard. It has createIssue :351, updateIssue :355, listIssues :360 and commentOnIssue :364 (packages/capabilities/src/githost/types.ts) but no comment edit (PATCH /issues/comments/:id), no comment get, no list of one issue's comments with updatedAt, author association and author type, no pin (GitHub pins only through the GraphQL pinIssue mutation on the issue's node id), no hasIssues on RepoInfo (:11-29) and no conditional read; IssueInfo (:83-90) has no author, node id, updatedAt or locked flag; CommentInfo (:92-98) has no updatedAt. No runtime code calls any issue method (a grep over packages and apps finds only types.ts, github.ts and memory.ts) (evidence: wave8-codemap.md 2.1 and R3).

[major, never cut] W8-host-2: The GitHub adapter reads one page and pays for every poll: listIssues reads one page of 100 with no paging (packages/capabilities/src/githost/github.ts:665-673); toIssue (:1298-1309) maps no user.login, updated_at, id or node_id and toComment no updated_at; request (:172-258) keeps no ETag and sends no If-None-Match, so each repeated read costs a rate-limit point (evidence: wave8-codemap.md 2.2).

[major, never cut] W8-host-3: The stand-in GitHub cannot test it: repoJson sets has_issues: true always (testenv/src/githost/store.ts:452), so issues off (410) never happens; GET /issues has no sort= (routes-issues.ts:46-66); no route answers 304 (cgi.ts:130 handles 304 for git http only); author_association is always 'OWNER' (design collab-07). There is no GraphQL endpoint at all (a grep for graphql in testenv/src finds only a rate-limit resource name, routes-app.ts:166) and no pinned issues: routes-projects.ts serves classic repository projects, columns and cards (:1-3), not Projects v2. The adapter posts GraphQL to graphqlUrlFor(baseUrl), '<base>/graphql' (packages/capabilities/src/githost/github.ts:150; github-graphql.ts:161-165), so the stand-in must answer POST /graphql at its own base; the pattern to copy is packages/capabilities/test/helpers/fake-projects-graphql.ts (operations dispatched on operationName, github-graphql.ts:1-7). No route reads a login's permission on a repository (collaborators are a plain set, fake-git-host.ts:176-180) (evidence: wave8-codemap.md 2.4, corrected; checked at c15d75e).

[major] W8-host-4: MemoryGitHost has no comment edit, no issue author, no pin and no ETag (packages/capabilities/src/githost/memory.ts:396-435; issues share nextNumber with pull requests, which stays) (evidence: wave8-codemap.md 2.3).

[minor] W8-host-5: The status issue and its writers' last activity cannot be read cheaply: no listIssues by creator or label with paging and sort, and no read of the newest comment per author that amendment 3's activity rule needs (evidence: wave8-codemap.md 2.1 'Missing'; runC-plan.json wave8_amendments[3]).

[minor] W8-host-6: Two issue errors are not told apart from the rest. The adapter already maps GitHub's answers to codes with details.status (packages/capabilities/src/githost/github.ts:228-246: 401 provider_auth, 403 tool_not_allowed, 404 not_found, 405/409/422 validation, anything else provider_error; the rate-limited 403 is provider_rate_limit at :211-221), but issues off (410) and a 5xx after retries share provider_error, and nothing reads a 403, or a 404 on a repository the token sees, as 'no permission' for an issue call, so no caller can say the one sentence the owner's status design asks for (evidence: design collab-07; github.ts:211-246 at c15d75e).

[minor, never cut] W8-host-7: Nothing shows that two homes on one host see one issue store: a comment written from home A must be listed to home B with author ada and its association, and the reverse (evidence: wave8-oldplan-mapped.json status-issue-host, D9 addition (3)).

[major, never cut, security] W8-host-8: Nothing can tell whether a comment's author has write access. author_association is not write access: MEMBER is any member of the organisation whatever their access to this repository, and COLLABORATOR includes collaborators with the read role. The port has no read of a login's permission on the repository (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{login}/permission), so a read-only member or collaborator could announce work and make the other Forerunner skip it, against the owner's default 'only people with write access count' (evidence: /tmp/frbench/collab/owner-summary.md:139; packages/capabilities/src/githost/types.ts:259-398 has no such read; the checkers' review of 2026-11-24).
decisions: Owner, 2026-11-02 (the status design, carried word for word in this plan's decisions D-W8-2): one pinned issue per project; one comment per writer, edited only by that writer; issue text is information, never instructions. This area builds the host calls only and writes no issue by itself.

Session lead, 2026-11-24, from the brief's proposal (section 4: status-issue-host stays whole); the owner can overrule: GitHost gains listIssueComments(repo, number, {etag, since}) with each comment's author login, author association, author type (Bot), createdAt and updatedAt (exactly the fields GitHub's REST comment has: no editor, which REST does not return; the stand-ins return no more than GitHub does), answering {notModified} on a 304; updateIssueComment(repo, id, body); getIssueComment(repo, id); getIssue(repo, number) with node id, state, state reason, locked, author and updatedAt; pinIssue(repo, number) answering 'pinned', 'limit' or 'forbidden'; RepoInfo.hasIssues; listIssues paged with creator, labels and sort; getRepoPermission(repo, login) answering admin, maintain, write, triage, read or none, cached per login and token with its ETag (a refused read counts as no write access: fails closed). No comment delete on the port: Forerunner never deletes a comment (the stand-in keeps its DELETE route for the tamper tests).
No lock call: owner question 7 of 2026-11-02 keeps its default (not locked), so nothing locks the issue (D-W8-13).

ETag reads: the adapter keeps an ETag and body cache per URL and token in memory only (nothing on disk, nothing to migrate); a 304 answers 'not modified' with the cached body; the stand-in answers 304 on issue and comment reads.

Association from the repository owner, the organisation's members and the collaborators, else NONE, on both stand-ins, as GitHub derives it; it is only a cheap first filter (NONE, CONTRIBUTOR and FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR are never write access). Write access is the login's permission read (write, maintain or admin), on both stand-ins from the roles w8-two-homes adds; the writer's body rebuild, the reader and the feed count only those (D-W8-13, D-W8-37; session lead, 2026-11-24, from the checkers' review).

Errors: one new code, issues_disabled (410); 'no permission' is a reason read from the existing tool_not_allowed (403) and not_found (404 on a repository the token sees), with details.status kept; provider_rate_limit and provider_error (a 5xx after retries: unavailable) stay as they are; callers turn each into one sentence.
The stand-ins let any login with write access PATCH any comment, as GitHub does (w8-status-write's tamper tests need it); Forerunner editing only its own comment is w8-status-write's rule.
u_entries: None of its own: host calls only; w8-status-write's U-entry covers what a person sees.

problems: [major, never cut] L4i-left-2: W15-01's sole-linked rule: an unmarked open fr/docs-scaffold (or fr/status) pull request of another project counts as this project's own when this project is the only one on this install linked to the repository, so the scaffold, Try again and the status writer write onto it. (evidence: Sources: L4i #55, #65, routing never_cut[1]. packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:236-247 isProjectDocsPr: a scaffold PR with no recorded pr_url, no hidden mark and no 'Forerunner project X.' line returns opts.soleLinked; :259-267 isProjectStatusPr does the same for fr/status; ownsUnmarkedDocs (:280-299) is true when this install's RepositoryIndex lists only this project for the repository. Callers: the scaffold write (:925-931), the status write (:1155-1160), the Overview listing (daemon/pull-requests.ts:411-416, :514). A together project is safe (isTogether returns false first). The L4i real-daemon Try again case wrote onto fr/docs-scaffold until Sandbox's PR body was marked.) Fix: Breaks wave 8's 'Never' rule (no write to another Forerunner's pull request). Another Forerunner's project is never in this install's index, so any non-together project here is always 'sole linked': an unmarked scaffold or status PR that the other Forerunner, a person or an older version opened is written onto. It fails open today. Fix: an unmarked PR is this project's only when this install recorded or opened it; otherwise it is nobody's (fails closed). Test with two composed homes against one stand-in GitHub (brief section 9). Area: repo-guide (the scaffold writer) in wave 8's first group; the fr/status half goes with status-issue-write, which replaces the status pull request. Code map 1.2 root cause: ownership of an open scaffold pull request is decided by its body alone, with 'this project is the only one linked here' as the fallback (packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:247); scaffoldBranchFor returns fr/docs-scaffold whenever a pull request is open (:971) and reads the branch's own .forerunner/project.json only when none is (:974-978); a take-over widens 'own' with the taken-over id (:287-291). The same fallback serves docsInPullRequests (:1323-1326) and the Pull requests list with Merge (daemon/pull-requests.ts:413-415, :512-515). This area fixes every write and the list; the fr/status half goes with the status pull request in w8-status-write (W8-write-5).

It touches the intake docs branch that brief section 5.3 re-decides for two Forerunners, so it goes with repo-guide. Medium.

(evidence: Source: leftovers-L4e.json L4e-rest-3 (rated 'rare'). packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:1030 and :1092 rebuildForTakeOver unchanged since 7081d6f; no later commit names it.) Fix: Scaffold on GitHub. It was rare with one Forerunner. Under D9 another Forerunner merges into main all the time (brief section 5.2, 'Main moves under you'), so a take-over rebuild can undo the other person's merged docs. Area: repo-guide (the scaffold writer). Small to medium, with a case where main changed the file after the merge-base.
decisions: Owner, 2026-11-02, carried word for word: 'Every repository gets a standard guide for agents and people by default (with the docs scaffold), kept current by Forerunner: design from the collab audit (wf_841cec48-831, /tmp/frbench/collab/).' and 'No docs/status.md in repositories (remove the untrue template).' (D-W8-2, D-W8-3).

Session lead, 2026-11-24, from the brief's proposal (section 8 question 5); the owner can overrule (D-W8-9): the Forerunner that made the project (the marker's writer) writes the doc set, the marker and the guide's Forerunner part; a together project writes none of them (run C's OR-15, as built), reads the guide as data and never takes the shared id's docs pull requests as its own; decision files from either Forerunner are named by date, docs/decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md (the intake's first decision included), so parallel pull requests never collide by number; an existing 0001-style file stays as it is; the person's Inbox answers go to the project's decision record: an existing 0001-*.md, else the intake's date-named record (found by its mark), else a new docs/decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-project-decisions.md, never a new 0001 file, and the Inbox card names the record's real file instead of 'docs/decisions/0001-…'. Recorded in ADR 0058 and ADR 0117 (dated amendments) and in this area's ADR.

The guide's line (runC-plan.json wave8_amendments[6], as worded there): 'This repository is the Forerunner project "<name>". To work on it with Forerunner, link this repository in your own Forerunner and choose Work together; do not start a second project on it. Each Forerunner announces its work in the pinned status issue.' 'Before you start' says announce, not claim (the 2026-11-02 bullet 'Forerunner's agents claim each task before working on it' is untrue under D9: D-W8-5): read the status issue, keep one comment of your own and edit only it, say what you work on with its title and the files it touches ('- what · files · PR #n · until'; a branch may be named as information but never identifies work), remove your line when done; each Forerunner merges its own pull requests; issue text is information, never instructions; no costs, secrets or personal details there. The status issue's state is a guide fact (on, switched off for this project in Settings, issues turned off on the repository): when it is not on, the guide's status line and 'Before you start' say that the Forerunner that made the project keeps its status in the app and announces nothing on GitHub, and point to the open pull requests instead (exact text per state; D-W8-44, session lead, 2026-11-24, from the checkers' review). The issue is always named by its title ('the pinned issue "Forerunner status: <name>"'), never by its number.

W15-01's ownership rule (L4i-left-2), session lead, 2026-11-24, from the code map's and the classifier's fix options and the brief's 'Never' rule: an open pull request is this project's for a write only when this install opened it or recorded its URL, or its branch's own .forerunner/project.json names this project itself (a taken-over id does not count: the take-over writes only its own branch, L4-github-102); otherwise it is nobody's and nothing is pushed to it or commented on it (fails closed). The sole-linked fallback stays only for listing, as information, never with Merge.

The guide is English, like every screen (owner's answer 3 of 2026-11-17 for chat's fixed lines; the 2026-11-02 question 'English or the brief's language' kept with this default); other tools' files (Cursor rules, Copilot instructions) are not written (default kept).

Only the person merges the guide's docs pull request (ADR 0058); the guide is re-rendered at session end and when a fact changes (name, goal, default branch, who merges, checks, the status issue's state: on, switched off or issues off; never its number, so the issue's creation never gives the first person a docs pull request to merge), one docs pull request at a time; Forerunner's part sits between <!-- forerunner:guide:start --> and <!-- forerunner:guide:end -->; an existing AGENTS.md keeps the person's text byte for byte; CLAUDE.md holds the one line '@AGENTS.md', or gets it as its first line once.

decisions: Owner, 2026-11-02, carried word for word (D-W8-2): 'GitHub issue page only: one pinned issue per project ('Forerunner status: <project>', hidden marker), summary rewritten after each session, 'Working on now' updated when a task starts and ends, each person/agent/install its own comment edited in place, read when a repository is connected (new or familiar), before planning and before every task, untrusted text never instructions, author marked, no costs; stays in the app with one sentence when issues are off / no permission / offline. No docs/status.md in repositories (remove the untrue template).'

Owner question 7 of 2026-11-02 (brief section 8 question 9; session lead, 2026-11-24, from the brief's proposal; the owner can overrule): not locked; only writers with write access count (the login's permission on the repository, w8-issue-host's W8-host-8; association is only a first filter, D-W8-37); on by default with a per-project off switch (Settings, W8-write-10); the Projects mirror's cost field dropped. One place holds these (statusIssuePolicy and the Settings row), so an answer changes one place.

Which issue a project writes (W8-write-9, D-W8-45; session lead, 2026-11-24, from the brief's proposal and the checkers' review; the owner can overrule): a project writes only the issue keyed by its own id (K), and only when the default branch's .forerunner/project.json names that id or names none yet; a together project shares the id, so it writes its own comment on issue K; a project here whose repository's marker names another project and which is not together writes no issue and no comment, and its status stays in the app with one sentence ('Status stays in the app: o/kite is the Forerunner project "Kite club"; Work together on the Overview shares its status issue.', proposal, exact text in the fixup); after a take-over the new project writes its own issue once its marker is on the default branch, never the old project's; a pair made here before the rule writes one issue, the project the marker names (or the kept one after Make one project). The join's only GitHub write is w8-together's call of closeOwnStatusPullRequest: the closing project wrote no issue under this rule.

The writer (D-W8-15, D-W8-35; session lead, 2026-11-24, from the brief's proposal and the checkers' review; the owner can overrule): the writer is this runtime's own device row (the install id; the cloud runner's runner row for the cloud runner) plus the GitHub login; compose registers the device row whenever it wires the status board (registerDevice gains that condition, compose.ts:6016), so a startServices: false compose has one; the comment's marker carries a non-reversible writer key, the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 over the device row id and K, never the row id itself; two installs with one login keep two comments; a reinstall is a new install id, and its old comment stays and reads 'not seen since' (Forerunner never edits or deletes it; the person may delete it on GitHub).

The issue: title 'Forerunner status: <project>'; first body line '<!-- forerunner:status v1 key=K -->'; label 'forerunner:status' when allowed; found by the stored number (project setting status_issue), then open issues carrying the marker, then the title; created by the first Forerunner that starts a task or ends a session on the repository, never because a repository was linked and never at the Work together press (OR-15); two creating at once: the lowest number wins and the other closes its own with one line; pinned while fewer than three issues are pinned, else left unpinned and Settings says so.

The comment: '<!-- forerunner:status-writer v1 key=K writer=<writer key> -->', created once and then only edited in place; header '**<agent name> (Forerunner)** · <login> · updated <time UTC>' (the agent's name as w8-shared-repo names it); sections Working on now ('- "Add a footer" · files footer.html · since 21:00 · until 22:30 UTC'; a branch only as information), Waiting for Merge ('- #12 "Write notes page" · files notes.html'), Paused (what is done and left, quoted from the handoff after redaction, and whether the project's checks pass on the kept work; a pause without progress reads as waiting for its owner's answer), Waiting for Claude (by the person's credential policy, D5 and D-W8-40: 'waits until 15:40, then it goes on' only when the policy is to wait and the session resumes by itself at the reset; under ask first 'waits for its person's answer' with no time; under go on with the next credential no wait line, since the session goes on; information, no Cancel), Last session ('Last session (2 Nov 20:59 UTC): did 1 task: "Write notes page". Next: "Add styles".'). Never in a comment or the body: money figures, chat words, Inbox answers, email addresses, secrets, @mentions or ids other than pull request numbers; the hidden markers are the one place an id appears (the project id K and the writer key, D-W8-35).

Redaction (session lead, 2026-11-24, from the checkers' review): every piece of free text a renderer quotes (the handoff, task titles, Next lines) passes one step, redactQuoted in status-board-words.ts, which removes money figures (a number beside CHF, USD, EUR, $, € or £), email addresses and @mentions (the @ dropped, the name kept) and nothing else; a title's own words stay ('Fix the cost page' is written as it is).

The body is a view rebuilt after each session (debounced 30 s; re-read and rebuilt at most twice when a comment changed after the snapshot) from the comments of writers that pass the one writer filter (D-W8-37: the author's write access, a valid marker and that login), never from any other comment; any such writer may rebuild it, so it outlives the Forerunner that made the project: 'Each person and agent keeps one comment below up to date; this summary is rebuilt from them. How to work here: AGENTS.md.'

When: task start (until = now + 90 min), every 30 minutes while the task runs, task end (the line goes; an accepted pull request moves to Waiting for Merge; a merged one goes), a pause, a credential wait, session end (Last session, then the body) and Quit (lines cleared, best effort). Writes coalesce: one pending text per writer and issue, kept in this install's store, sent once when GitHub answers; reads use the ETag.

Tamper and loss: this writer's comment is known by its stored id, its login and its writer key; because GitHub's REST comment names no editor, an edit by anyone is found by comparing the comment's body with the text this writer last sent (kept in its own store); a changed body is restored once and the person told once (the restore is on the cut line, as in the 2026-11-02 plan); deleted: recreated; a comment by another login carrying this writer key is that login's, is never edited by this writer and fails the writer filter; Forerunner never edits another writer's comment; a closed issue is not reopened ('The status issue #12 was closed on GitHub; reopen it there to use it again.'); a deleted issue gets one new issue and the person is told once.

When GitHub cannot be written, the status stays in the app with one sentence (Docs tab and Settings): 'Status stays in the app: issues are turned off on owner/repo.'; 'Status stays in the app: Forerunner may not write issues on owner/repo (the GitHub key needs Issues: read and write).'; 'Status on GitHub: last updated 14:05; it updates when GitHub answers.'; a refused pin leaves the issue working unpinned. Settings: 'Status on GitHub: issue #12 (pinned)' with the off switch (W8-write-10: off, this install writes no issue or comment for the project and the app's status stays: 'Status stays in the app: the status issue is turned off for "Team site" in Settings.', proposal), and on a public repository 'Everyone who can see this repository can read it.'; the Docs tab: 'In the app; also on GitHub: issue #12'.

The status pull request goes (amendment 2). An open status pull request an earlier version of this install opened for this project (its mark and this install's record) is closed by this install with one line; never one of another project or an unmarked one. U-087 is closed as superseded. Session lead, 2026-11-24.

[major, never cut] W8-read-2 (NW-1; amendment 4): Announced work cannot be matched. The watcher sees the default head move each minute (session/githost-watcher.ts:587-620, DEFAULT_GITHOST_POLL_MS :61) but compose only refreshes the copy (daemon/compose.ts:2820); nothing records what was merged since the last plan, and a task's brief has no 'merged since' section (session/task-context.ts:331-443), so done work can be redone (evidence: brief 5.2; wave8-codemap.md 4.4 and R5).

decisions: Owner, 2026-11-02 (carried, D-W8-2): read when a repository is connected (new or familiar), before planning and before every task; untrusted text never instructions; author marked; announcements, not locks.

Session lead, 2026-11-24, from the brief's proposals (section 8 questions 2, 3 and 4) and the checkers' review; the owner can overrule (D-W8-6, D-W8-7, D-W8-8, D-W8-38): announcements in the status issue, never locks (hard claims through GitHub issue assignees stay the alternative only if the journey shows collisions); an announcement carries the task's title and the files it touches; code matches by files before the claim: every file of this task in another writer's fresh announcement: skipped with 'left to bob's Forerunner: announced on GitHub'; some files shared: a heads-up line in this writer's comment and the log, then work goes on and the branch is brought up to date before its pull request (F.5); a task that names no file is matched by title only in the planner's data, never by code; the planner sees titles and files as data and leaves the work out; no extra model call; a branch never matches. Freshness is bounded by GitHub's own time, not the writer's text or clock: a Working on now line is fresh only while its comment's GitHub updated_at is within 60 minutes (twice the 30-minute refresh) and its 'until' has not passed; a Paused line holds its task only while its writer was seen (the comment's GitHub updated_at) within the 14-day activity window; otherwise either reads 'not seen since <date>' and blocks nothing (the planner may still see it as data). Two at once: the announcement whose edit GitHub stamped earlier keeps the work (each writer records the updated_at its own edit returned and compares it, right after that edit, with the other comment's updated_at; never the comment's created time); the later home stops before its first commit, says so in one line ('bob's Forerunner announced "X" first; nothing was done here.'), the task waits for the next plan and is not counted as done.

Only writers that pass the one writer filter announce (D-W8-37): the author's permission on the repository is write, maintain or admin (w8-issue-host's getRepoPermission, cached per login with its ETag; association OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR is only a first filter, since MEMBER and COLLABORATOR include read-only people), the comment carries a valid marker, and its author is the login it names; any other line is a note (owner question 7 of 2026-11-02, default kept, D-W8-13). Issue text can only make Forerunner more careful: it never merges, deletes, runs a command, opens a site, changes a setting or starts a session; a branch named on the issue is never built on (the other Forerunner's branches are never this store's dependency).

The plan-only block gains lines inside the existing data markers, quoted and neutralised as the tasks are: 'Announced on GitHub by bob's Forerunner: "X" (files a, b)' and 'Merged on GitHub: "Y" (files c)'; every brief gets a 'Merged on GitHub since your last session' section in taskContextBlock with JSON-quoted data, as the previous attempt's section is (task-context.ts:419-424). The 'merged since' mark is persisted per project. Both are capped: at most 10 announced and 10 merged lines, newest first, the rest as one count line ('and 4 more merged on GitHub since your last session.', exact text), and the section's tokens are counted in the estimate the person is shown (session lead, 2026-11-24, from the checkers' review).

Merged work is read from pull requests carrying the project's mark merged since the mark (the listPullRequests read with state all that run C makes); a push straight to the default branch without a pull request is not seen (ADR 0117's limit, kept; D-W8-27).
Duplicates by meaning only (other files, same intent) are a live-check step of the final check (F-W8-2), never a promise (design section 5 rule 9).

The take-over's activity (amendment 3): the open issue of key K and its writers' newest comments join the pull requests' updatedAt in the 14-day rule; the offer names who works there and when last ('by ada, last active 21 Nov'); this install's own login never blocks Take it over; Work together stays the first button.

L4i-left-48 and -65 are built in w8-together (D-W8-22, moved on the checkers' review); this area's read before planning goes inside the background planning that area builds, so Add to never waits on GitHub.

GitHub text that reaches a model prompt has an injection case per path (D-W8-39; session lead, 2026-11-24, from the checkers' review): the status comment, a merged pull request's title and files (the plan-only block and every brief), and the work-in-progress commit message the other agent's handoff is quoted from (pr-executor.ts:833-858 writes 'Where I stopped:' and 'Left to do' verbatim); each is quoted inside the data markers, flagged to the person when the scan flags it, and nothing is acted on.

GitHub text is data, never instructions: issue comments, pull request titles and bodies, commit messages, marker names and branch names are parsed strictly, passed through the injection scan (packages/runtime/src/injection/scan.ts, wrapUntrusted), quoted and never acted on; a card or Updates line that quotes such text is a record for chat (quotesOthersWords, D-W8-39); a comment counts only from an author with write access (D-W8-37) and can only make Forerunner more careful; GitHub is read with the configured host and token only.

No money on GitHub, no budget passed: no cost, cap, spend or CHF/USD figure in anything this area writes to GitHub; no budget, cap or wrap-up line is passed or changed; reading GitHub costs no model money; each person's spend stays on their own ledger.

Words by design section 5 (docs/design/core-experience.md): names, not ids ('bob's Forerunner', task titles in quotes; never an install id, device id, task id, comment id or UUID on a screen or in any text GitHub shows; the one exception is the hidden HTML markers, which carry only the project id and a non-reversible writer key, and every 'no ids' check skips exactly those marker lines, D-W8-35); no costs, emails or chat on GitHub, commit authors and committers included (D-W8-36); 'you' only for the person looking; no promise beyond what is built (run C stops at 'each keeps its own tasks'); every new sentence tested as exact text and listed in notes_for_other_areas with old and new text.

Never write to, comment on, close, merge or rebuild another Forerunner's pull request, or rewrite its marker, guide part or status comment: each two-home case asserts the stand-in host's request log (writesBy(login)) shows no such write from either home.

areas.title: You see what the other Forerunner does, read from GitHub within about a minute: its status comment and its pull requests as information, one Updates line per session of it, and never a Merge or Stop on its work or a word of its spend
problems: [major, never cut] W8-feed-1 (amendment 9): The other Forerunner's work never reaches the person: run C shows only 'Shared on GitHub with another Forerunner: each keeps its own tasks.' (TOGETHER_OVERVIEW_LINE, packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-words.ts:275); the Peers section and the Inbox read this store only (session/peers.ts:104); nothing shows another writer's status comment (working on now, waiting for Merge, paused work, credential waits, last session) (evidence: walk C-19; runC-plan.json wave8_amendments[9]).

[major, never cut] W8-feed-2 (amendment 9; brief section 9 'Never'): The other Forerunner's pull requests on the project (its project mark with task marks this install does not own) are not listed. When listed they must be information with Open on GitHub only: no Merge, no Stop, no link to a page this computer cannot open; the merge loop, the take-out, the conflict notices and the watcher keep acting only through this install's task rows (daemon/pull-requests.ts:376 lists open pull requests and matches a row only by branch or pr_url :462; session/githost-watcher.ts:211-235) (evidence: brief section 3; wave8-codemap.md 1.1).

[major, never cut] W8-feed-3 (C7, rewritten for D9): What waits for Merge is invisible to the other side: buildPeerFeed counts only in_review tasks as open pull requests (session/peers.ts:129-136) and a done task's claim is cleared, so with the default 'you press Merge' every accepted task waits unseen; the other Forerunner's open pull requests and their files must feed this install's overlap check (F.6 across Forerunners) (evidence: code C7, design collab-05).

[major] W8-feed-4 (collab-live): Nothing brings the other Forerunner's changes to the screen: /events relays only this process's events; the watcher polls every 60 s (DEFAULT_GITHOST_POLL_MS, githost-watcher.ts:61) only task rows with a pr_url (:211-235) and the default head (:587-620), so another writer's comment change or merged pull request would show only after a reload (evidence: walk C-10; wave8-codemap.md 4.4).

[minor] W8-feed-5: The person hears nothing when the other Forerunner's session ends; under D9 the handoff is the writer comment's Last session, and it should reach the Inbox as at most one Updates line per session of the other Forerunner, never one per change and never with a spend (evidence: brief section 6; design collab-12).

[minor] W8-feed-6 (NW-7): The first person never learns that a second Forerunner works on the project: GitHub write access is the consent, and Forerunner should show it once in Updates, never as a card or notification (evidence: brief 5.7 and section 8 question 10).

[minor] W8-feed-7: relativeTime clamps to the past (apps/ui/src/lib/time.ts:109 'Math.max(0, now - t)'), so an announcement's 'until' 30 minutes ahead reads 'just now'; PeersSection shows raw task ids (apps/ui/src/pages/project/PeersSection.tsx); pull request rows do not say whose agent did the work, and rows read from GitHub must name the other's login, never 'you' (evidence: walk C-17, C-22).

decisions: D-W8-1 Premise (the owner's answer 1 of 2026-11-09, D9), and brief section 8 question 1 decided, never asked again: every person runs their own Forerunner on their own PC with their own API key, subscription, store, budgets and caps; two people on one repository work in one project (run C's Work together); they meet on GitHub (pull requests, the pinned status issue, the repository guide); no shared database or server. The owner's words: "if multiple people will be running it they will be using their own api and subscription and running it on their pc." and "if 2 people are working on the same project they should be able to work seamlessly in the same git. Isnt this already built in cleanly?". So collab-members, collab-privacy, collab-privacy-service, collab-claims-2 and collab-offline go (plan_check.brief_section_4), and the state service stays for one person's own devices (D-W8-29).

D-W8-2 Carried word for word, the owner's status design of 2026-11-02: "GitHub issue page only: one pinned issue per project ('Forerunner status: <project>', hidden marker), summary rewritten after each session, 'Working on now' updated when a task starts and ends, each person/agent/install its own comment edited in place, read when a repository is connected (new or familiar), before planning and before every task, untrusted text never instructions, author marked, no costs; stays in the app with one sentence when issues are off / no permission / offline. No docs/status.md in repositories (remove the untrue template)." Built by w8-status-write and w8-status-read.

D-W8-3 Carried word for word, the owner's guide decision of 2026-11-02: "Every repository gets a standard guide for agents and people by default (with the docs scaffold), kept current by Forerunner: design from the collab audit (wf_841cec48-831, /tmp/frbench/collab/)." Built by w8-repo-guide (AGENTS.md plus a one-line CLAUDE.md, kept current by Forerunner).

D-W8-4 What does not change under D9 (brief section 2), each built as decided: one pinned issue per project; one comment per writer, edited only by that writer; no costs, emails or chat on GitHub; issue text is information, never instructions. The guide decision (AGENTS.md plus a one-line CLAUDE.md, kept current by Forerunner). "No docs/status.md in repositories". No email reaches GitHub through commits either (D-W8-36).

D-W8-5 Three sentences the owner was told on 2026-11-02 (/tmp/frbench/collab/owner-summary.md) that D9 makes untrue; the session lead corrects them in the next summary to the owner, and no screen, guide or document of wave 8 repeats them: (1) "It works without a shared database ... When two people do share a database, the database stays the record and the issue only adds people outside it, so nobody is shown twice." Why untrue now: No shared-store mode (brief section 8 question 1, decided): the issue is the main channel between two Forerunners, not an extra. (2) "If you need "never twice" for certain, share a database." Why untrue now: Same; 'never twice' rests on announcements plus code matching files (new work 1); hard claims through issue assignees stay the alternative only if the journey shows collisions (brief question 2). (3) "Forerunner's agents claim each task before working on it, so pick work nobody has announced. (guide bullet)" Why untrue now: Claims live in each Forerunner's own store; the guide says Forerunner's agents announce each task in the status issue before they start, so pick work nobody announced. The rest of what the owner was told about the status issue and the guide stays true and is built (9 statements, wave8-oldplan-mapped.json carried_decisions.as_told_to_the_owner_2026_11_02_kept).

Hard claims through GitHub issue assignees stay the alternative only if the journey or the live check shows collisions. Announcements stay announcements: every line, Paused lines included, lapses ('not seen since', blocks nothing) once GitHub's own time says its writer went quiet (D-W8-38). Built by w8-status-read (W8-read-2, -3).
